evidence.title: Fed Gets Fresh Inflation Signal From U.S. Businesses
evidence.body: [e001:f01] Businesses 1 min read QQQ U.S. businesses expect inflation pressures to ease slightly over the coming year, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's latest survey, offering another modest sign that cost expectations are cooling. [e001:f02] Year-ahead business inflation expectations fell to 2.3% in October from 2.4% in September , according to the Atlanta Fed's Business Inflation Expectations survey. [e001:f03] The decline continues a substantial retreat from the 3.8% peak reached in April 2022 . [e001:f04] But inflation expectations have not completely normalized. [e001:f05] The current 2.3% reading remains above the 2.0% average recorded between January 2017 and December 2019 , suggesting businesses still expect somewhat stronger cost pressures than they did before the pandemic. [e001:f06] There is another complication. [e001:f07] Uncertainty surrounding companies' year-ahead unit costs has increased since reaching a low of 1.9% in February, indicating businesses have become less confident about exactly where their costs are heading. [e001:f08] Longer-term expectations also remain elevated across most major industries compared with pre-pandemic levels. [e001:f09] That distinction matters because businesses often make pricing, hiring and investment decisions partly on where they expect labor and input costs to move. [e001:f10] The survey offered a potentially encouraging signal from the labor market as well. [e001:f11] Looking 12 months ahead, the average business expects monthly turnover to decline by roughly two percentage points to 5.6% . [e001:f12] Investor Takeaway I think the October report is mildly encouraging for the inflation outlook, but it does not give the Federal Reserve an all-clear. [e001:f13] The drop to 2.3% from 2.4% suggests near-term cost expectations are moving in the right direction. [e001:f14] For investors, that means the Fed will likely care more about whether this trend continues alongside actual inflation data rather than reacting strongly to one monthly survey. [e001:f15] The key things to watch are business cost expectations, wage growth, employee turnover, upcoming inflation readings and whether longer-run expectations begin moving closer to their pre-pandemic averages . [e001:f16] For now, businesses are expecting slightly less inflation.
